;Armed conflicts and attacks
*Suspected [[Islamist]] militants kill at least 62 civilians in a series of massacres in eastern [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] as killings of civilians intensify. The country's [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|armed forces]] launch counter-offensives against [[insurgent]]s of the [[Allied Democratic Forces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-violence/militants-kill-dozens-in-east-congo-as-attacks-on-civilians-intensify-idUSKBN1ZV3OS (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*400–500 people are left stranded at the [[Sasquatch Mountain Resort]] in [[British Columbia]], [[Canada]], after the road to the resort was damaged from landslides caused by heavy rain. Train service between [[Vancouver]] and [[Seattle]] was also suspended until Monday due to mudslides. [https://bc.ctvnews.ca/landslide-washouts-strand-500-people-on-sasquatch-mountain-ski-hill-1.4793567 (CTV News)] [https://bc.ctvnews.ca/mudslide-means-passenger-trains-between-vancouver-and-seattle-won-t-resume-until-monday-1.4793612 (CTV News²)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Kiribati]] becomes the latest country in the Pacific to block [[Chinese people|Chinese]] travelers by placing all [[travel visa|visa]] applications from [[China]] on hold and ordering all those coming from countries with confirmed cases of the virus to self-[[quarantine]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/408618/coronavirus-kiribati-blocks-chinese-travellers (Radio NZ International)]
**[[Apple Inc.]] announces it will close all of its stores and offices in China until February 9 due to the pandemic. [https://gizmodo.com/apple-is-closing-all-of-its-stores-and-corporate-office-1841410459 (''Gizmodo'')]

;International relations
*[[2020 Trump Israel–Palestine plan|Trump peace plan]]
**The [[Palestinian National Authority]] cuts all ties with the [[United States]] and [[Israel]], including those relating to security, after rejecting a peace plan presented by [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-palestinians-security/palestinian-authority-cuts-ties-with-israel-and-u-s-idUSKBN1ZV3PO (Reuters)]
*[[Foreign relations of the Maldives]]
** The [[Maldives]] returns to the [[Commonwealth of Nations]] as a [[republic in the Commonwealth of Nations]]. [https://thecommonwealth.org/media/news/maldives-becomes-54th-member-commonwealth-family (The Commonwealth)]

;Law and crime
*A court in [[Egypt]] sentences a former special forces officer and 36 others to the [[capital punishment in Egypt|death penalty]] after being convicted on charges of [[terrorism in Egypt|terrorism]], court officials say. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-egypt-security/egypt-sentences-officer-turned-militant-and-36-others-to-death-idUSKBN1ZV3IW (Reuters)]
*Police in [[South Africa]] launch a manhunt for the killers of nine illegal [[miner]]s who were stoned to death in western [[Johannesburg]]. All nine killed were from [[Lesotho]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-51341567 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019–2021 Iraqi protests]]
**Former Communications Minister [[Mohammed Tawfiq Allawi]] is appointed [[Prime Minister of Iraq]] by [[President of Iraq|President]] [[Barham Salih]]. Protestors reject his appointment, seeing him as part of the establishment. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/iraq-president-appoints-mohammed-allawi-pm-state-tv-200201150554113.html (Al Jazeera)]
